feedback: No race has run yet, so this feedback rests on the contract and on your stated intent, not on earlier outcomes. There is no earlier iteration to cite; this is iteration 0. Your choice of a symmetric five-sensor array with 12 mm footprints at 10 mm spacing covers the 25 mm tape with about 40 mm of span, so the signal should not saturate on the tape. The 0.04 m lookahead is short enough that a proportional-plus-derivative law should handle it. I used the same weight pattern on both sides, so the integrator has not yet needed any asymmetric compensation. Next race: if line_loss_events is above zero on the slalom, widen the span (for example x = ±0.025 m) before changing the lookahead. If steering_oscillation is high and rms_error is low, keep the geometry and have the integrator adjust gains instead. If completion fails on the sharpest bends with max_error near the off-track limit, try moving the array forward toward y = 0.05 to 0.06 m for more reaction time. Reserve the lighter-mass idea until the race shows whether turning authority is limiting.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events > 0 on the slalom, widen the sensor span from 0.04 m to about 0.05 m (x = ±0.025 m) while keeping five sensors and the 12 mm footprint.
If the run goes off track on the sharpest bend, move the array forward from y = 0.04 m to about 0.05 to 0.06 m, which gives more lookahead without changing the span.
Keep the current geometry if the race completes with low rms_error and little line loss, and report the completion_time so the Integrator can judge whether base_speed can rise.
